about: The repository's expected settings (greenrepo UPK-15), by the field names of GitHub's REST API, grouped by the
endpoint that reads them. `reader` is whose login can: `workflow`, the health workflow's own token, compared
weekly into the health issue; `admin`, the maintainer's, compared in the monthly session with
`bun scripts/health.ts --admin`. Only the fields named are compared; drift is reported, never applied. The
rulesets are in rulesets/, as GitHub exports them; the secrets and deploy keys are checked against renewals.toml.

settings.about: Public; issues open, pull requests from collaborators (GR-D2, GR-D5), into dev, the default branch (D251); Discussions for questions and ideas (GR-D17); no wiki or projects
Squash merges titled by the pull request, branches deleted (GR-D6); auto-merge per pull request, once its checks pass; secret scanning, security updates
Vulnerabilities reported privately, as SECURITY.md says (COM-06)
The `release` environment, holding the tap's deploy key, reached only by the refs it names (REL-07)
GitHub Pages built by a workflow (pages.yml), at the address the installer is run from (GR-D14)
The `github-pages` environment, which pages.yml deploys through, reached only by the refs it names
Pages deployed from `main` (by hand, the bootstrap changed), `test` (a preview), `v*` tags (a release)
Dependabot alerts on (DEP-01); GitHub answers 204 when they are, 404 when not
CodeQL's default setup, with the workflows (`actions`) among its languages (CI-12)
Actions on, each action pinned by its full commit hash (SET-06)
The workflow token read-only by default, unable to approve pull requests (SET-02)
A published release's assets and tag locked (REL-05)
No webhooks; one added is listed here, with its secret (SET-07)
The maintainer signs in with two factors (SET-01); GitHub shows it to its owner, with read:user
